title: Improving Access to Fertility Preservation for Young Cancer Patients
what_it_is: Improving Access to Fertility Preservation for Young Cancer Patients

sections.label: Young cancer patients in Singapore
sections.summary: About six in 100 cancer patients diagnosed yearly in Singapore are under 40, averaging 340 young men and 620 young women from 2017 to 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: About six out of 100 cancer patients diagnosed each year in Singapore are under the age of 40.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: If you look at the Singapore Cancer Registry, between 2017 and 2021, each year, on average, 340 young men and 620 young women under the age of 40 were diagnosed with cancer – about 1,000 young men and women.

sections.label: Fertility treatment not under MediShield Life
sections.summary: Fertility related treatments, even for cancer patients, are not covered under MediShield Life because they are not considered basic healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In short, today, fertility related treatments, even for cancer patients, are not covered under MediShield Life because these are not considered part of basic healthcare.

sections.label: Interest-free loans for fertility preservation
sections.summary: The third recommendation calls on the Government and MAS to work with banks and financial institutions to provide interest-free loans for young cancer patients needing fertility preservation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The third recommendation: I also call upon the Government and MAS to work together with the banks and financial institutions to provide interest-free loans for young cancer patients needing fertility preservation.

sections.label: Tax deduction for fertility preservation fund
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the existing 250% tax deduction on charitable donations can be enhanced for designated charities or a fertility preservation fund co-managed by MOH.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: For example, can the existing 250% tax deduction on charitable donations be enhanced further for specific designated charities or even a specific fund for fertility preservation that could be co-managed by MOH or the health authorities in the public sector?

sections.label: Singapore's falling total fertility rate
sections.summary: Singapore's total fertility rate has dropped to 0.97, below 1.0 for the first time in its history, making the message sent all the more important.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In an era of fewer children being born, when Singapore's total fertility rate (TFR) has dropped to 0.97, the TFR below 1.0 for the first time in Singapore's history, the message we send is all the more important.

sections.label: Government co-funding and MediSave for fertility
sections.summary: A Singaporean citizen couple can get up to 75% Government co-funding for three fresh and three frozen cycles, plus MediSave use up to $15,000 lifetime.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Today, a Singaporean citizen couple can enjoy up to 75% in Government co-funding for up to three fresh cycles and three frozen cycles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: On top of co-funding, we allow MediSave use of up to $6,000 for the first cycle, $5,000 for the second cycle and $4,000 for the third and subsequent cycles, with a lifetime limit of $15,000.

sections.label: Study fertility treatment co-funding proposals
sections.summary: MOH will study Dr Tan's proposals to extend Government co-funding and insurance for fertility treatments, noting other conditions besides cancer may affect fertility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: MOH will study Dr Tan's proposals to extend Government co-funding and insurance, bearing in mind there may be other medically necessary treatments for conditions besides cancer that could affect fertility of young Singaporeans.

sections.label: Interest-free loans and co-funding review
sections.summary: Government notes interest-free loans are financed and subsidised by Government like existing co-funding, will review co-funding adequacy, and welcomes charity support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As for the suggestion of interest-free loans, like the Tuition Fee loans, we note that these are ultimately financed and subsidised by Government, similar to the co-funding support that is currently already available for AR treatments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We will, however, continue to review the adequacy of co-funding and other support to address the fertility treatments for these patients and welcome any additional support that charities can provide alongside, to address affordability issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Pursuant to Standing Order 2(3)(a), I wish to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 11.00 am.
